clue.text: Study the sound of birds' in. Northern Europe

definitions.note: the clue's place name stands for the adjective describing that region

parts.note: to scan is to study closely
a din is a loud sound
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A scholar studying birdsong somewhere in the far north of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the region itself, with 'in' joining it to the wordplay; the answer is the adjective for the countries of Northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway, Sweden and Denmark make up the Nordic block of that part of the continent.

clue.text: Unter den Linden' is imposing

parts.note: German unter means under, as does the Latin prefix sub
linden is another name for the lime tree

explanation.surface: Berlin's famous boulevard, Unter den Linden, is grand and impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Unter den Linden is a grand avenue in Berlin, literally 'under the limes'; 'den' (the) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sublime is awe-inspiring and majestic, just as an imposing sight is.

clue.text: A giant set of maps

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth a Titan who held up the heavens

explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who carried the sky gave his name to a book of charts, often shown on its cover bearing a globe.

clue.text: Action taken about discourse being belittled

indicators.note: the letters for action go round the letters for discourse

parts.note: a deed is an action taken
a tract is a written discourse or treatise

explanation.surface: Measures taken over some speech were disparaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to diminish or disparage it, so detracted means made to seem less.

clue.text: An emperor in his ermine robe

indicators.note: the word in shows the answer sits inside the words ermine robe

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler dressed in his ceremonial fur-trimmed robe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman ruler famously said to have fiddled while the city burned.

clue.text: Lively but evil lot — a curious mixture

indicators.note: a curious mixture tells us the letters of the preceding words are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone describes a crowd as both spirited and wicked, an odd combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious mixture' shuffles EVIL LOT A into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile temperament is changeable and full of energy.

clue.text: Generous politician getting, in beer

indicators.note: the politician's letters are placed in the drink's letters

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A big-hearted politician gets stuck into the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ample portion is a generous, plentiful one.

clue.text: Not altogether content about bearing standard

indicators.note: the letters for content go round the others

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy, make content
E is east, a compass bearing
par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: Someone not entirely satisfied with a standard of behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: SATE is split around EPAR, giving S-EPAR-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept apart rather than together are distinct and divided.

clue.text: A rigid back

parts.note: stern means strict, rigid

explanation.surface: A stiff back, as of someone sitting bolt upright.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, astern means towards the rear.

clue.text: Act about a rate-change where two parties are involved

indicators.note: the letters for act go round the shuffled letters

parts.note: an Act of Parliament starts as a bill

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of a rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A law concerning a change in a rate negotiated between two sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns A RATE into ATERA, which goes inside BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral talks or agreements are those between two sides.

clue.text: Reporters cause a crowd

explanation.surface: Journalists gather in a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: The press means journalists collectively, and also a crush of people pushing together.

clue.text: Position for 'sophisticated and virtuous man — a local leader

parts.note: in can mean fashionable, sophisticated
St is short for saint, a virtuous man

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leader, or first letter, of local is L

explanation.surface: A post for a refined and upright person, perhaps a community head.
explanation.walkthrough: INSTAL is a variant spelling of install; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone is to set them in a post or place.

clue.text: Poor sailors' accommodation

parts.note: reads as cramped crew quarters, but means the cheapest passenger section of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Third-class quarters on an old ship were the cheapest berths, near the rudder gear.

clue.text: French art gallery's assets

parts.note: in French, tu es means thou art
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A Paris gallery's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous London art gallery; 'French art' means the French for 'art' as in 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's estate is all their property and possessions.

clue.text: The non-male falling for exercise

indicators.note: non-male says to take out the male pronoun from the word before

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Women dropping in for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-male' strips HE from THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical training is regular exercise to get fit.

clue.text: Fruit worker in basic housing

indicators.note: housing means the plain letters enclose the worker

parts.note: plain means basic, simple
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A fruit picker living in simple accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy cooking banana is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Possibly turn it on about one to prepare food

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the letter for one
possibly suggests the following letters may be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Switching on the cooker to make a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns TURN IT ON into NUTRTION, which goes about I; 'to prepare' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, what we eat to live.

clue.text: The firm left to slip into bankruptcy

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A company falls into insolvency.
explanation.definitionFit: A business failing completely is said to go under, its finances in ruin.

clue.text: Opening some returns to do with gold

indicators.note: returns means the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some
taken as written
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A partial refund to do with gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatch in a floor or ceiling is an entrance hole.

clue.text: Place of worship — the Head uses two

definitions.meaning: the head has one on each side of the brow

explanation.surface: A school head needs two places to pray.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine building is one sense; the flat side of the forehead, one either side, is the other.

clue.text: A West Country town will show the way

definitions.meaning: a small town in Somerset, south-west England

explanation.surface: Directions offered by a town in the south-west.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset, in England's West Country, home of Clarks shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somerset town shares its name with an ordinary road.

clue.text: Means of riot-control that's sure to affect the viewers

definitions.text: Means of riot-control that's sure to affect the viewers

parts.words: Means of riot-control that's sure to affect the viewers
parts.note: a crowd-dispersing chemical that makes the eyes stream

explanation.definitionFit: Police use an irritant spray to scatter crowds by making their eyes water.

clue.text: Bringing someone to doctor sick animal

parts.note: man means a person, someone
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Taking a person to see a doctor about an ailing pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A large brightly faced baboon is a primate.

clue.text: No railwaymen get up and talk incessantly

indicators.note: get up in a down clue tells us the letters are read upwards

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

explanation.surface: Railway workers refuse to rise and keep talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was the British National Union of Railwaymen; 'get up' turns NO NUR upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on and on is to keep speaking without a stop.

clue.text: A midday rest is a set arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of is a set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lunchtime nap is a fixed fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style afternoon nap taken in the heat of the day.

clue.text: Not moving yet

explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless and also nevertheless, as in 'still, I went'.

clue.text: Appear to understand-a large number

parts.note: to see is to understand
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Seeming to grasp a great many things.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the impression of being something.

clue.text: Pole after a row? That's material

indicators.note: the pole comes after the row

parts.note: a line is a row
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish worker after an argument wonders about cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax.

clue.text: Giving directions for quiet living

parts.note: p, piano, means quiet in music
residing means living in a place

explanation.surface: Advice on how to live a peaceful life.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chairing a meeting is in charge, steering it.

clue.text: Mixes in' time with single characters

parts.note: a term is a period of time

indicators.note: characters suggests the letters of single, shuffled

explanation.surface: A party host blends in some time with unattached people.
explanation.definitionFit: Blends together, as in a crowd.
